test_title: PYST 37: Selection Post (Matric Level) - GA (Held On 4 Aug 2022 Shift 1)
subject: gk
question: Which Fundamental Right was added through the 86th Constitutional Amendment, 2002?

options.text: To value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture
The parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education of his/her child/ward between the age of six and fourteen years.
To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India

solution:
The correct answer is __**The parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education of his/her child/ward between the age of six and fourteen years**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Right to Education** was made a **Fundamental Right** by the **86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002**.
 
• **Part IV** of The Indian Constitution, **Article 45** and **Article 39 (f)** of DPSP, had the provision for equitable and accessible education.
 
• The Right to Education serves as a building block to ensure that every child has his/her right to get a quality education between the age of **six** and** fourteen** years.
 
• In **1993**, the Supreme Court’s judgment in the **Unnikrishnan JP vs State of Andhra Pradesh & Others** held that Education is a fundamental right.
 
• **Tapas Majumdar Committee (1999)** was set up, which comprehend the insertion of **Article 21A**.
 
• The 86th amendment provided legislation for the Right to Education Bill 2008 and finally the Right to Education Act 2009.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 21-A, Right to Education:** The State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years in such manner as the State may, by law, determine.
 
• It had a clause for '**No Detention Policy'** which has been removed under **The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (Amendment) Act, 2019.**
 
• The act mandates 25% reservations for SC's and ST's , Socially Backward Class and Differently abled.
 
• It also focuses on making children free of fear, trauma, and anxiety through a system of child-friendly and child-centred learning.
